decisions.reason: As a renamed and evidently well-received evolution of an existing trommel screen, it builds directly on the firm's installed knowledge base and shows enough early acceptance to justify further refinement rather than withdrawal.

A mobile high-speed flail shredder fits closely with the firm's core recycling-machinery capabilities, and a dedicated product page suggests sufficient commitment and absorptive capacity to improve it after launch.

Although only briefly mentioned, a mobile high-speed grinder remains technologically close to the firm's established shredding and processing know-how, so management would more likely continue learning and adjust the offer than exit quickly.

The stationary electric fine shredder is adjacent to the firm's existing mechanical-processing expertise and likely benefits from in-house engineering and customer feedback, making retention more likely than discontinuation.

This green-waste grinder is a narrower variant in a familiar product family, so despite somewhat higher rationalisation risk from overlap, the firm would probably keep it on the market while it assimilates early application-specific demand information.

Stationary single-shaft pre-shredders are strongly aligned with the firm's long-developed waste and recycling equipment competences, and the dedicated presentation indicates a serious platform the firm is likely to continue supporting.
